title: CLI-Anything — personal fork
goal: Keep a low-drift personal integration fork of CLI-Anything that can absorb upstream improvements while carrying explicitly inventoried Kombiz-owned CLI harnesses.

state.plain: CLI-Anything is a large upstream collection of command-line harnesses that make desktop and server software usable by agents. This fork keeps upstream code on a clean `main` mirror and reserves `personal/main` plus inventoried topic branches for Kombiz-owned additions.
state.summary: The personal integration branch contains the explicit fork policy but is 15 upstream commits behind the clean mirror and one fork-policy commit ahead. Its personal CLI inventory is empty, while a completed Buzz topic branch has not yet been integrated. The Pages workflow consumes DigitalOcean Spaces credentials through GitHub Actions secrets, but immutable homelab-secrets references could not be resolved from the untrusted agent context. Registry identity remains unmatched because the similarly named Greymatter entry does not identify a GitHub repository.
narrative: The upstream project provides many independently packaged harnesses, root skill mirrors, a CLI-Hub registry, and a GitHub Pages publishing pipeline. Because most paths remain upstream-owned, the fork policy makes ownership explicit instead of treating every file in the fork as locally authored.

The clean `main` branch follows upstream. Personal changes start from `personal/main`, live on a focused `personal/<slug>` branch, and merge back only after review. `PERSONAL_CLIS.json` is the authoritative list of paths owned by the fork; it is intentionally empty on the current integration branch.

A Buzz harness has been implemented and reviewed on `personal/buzz`, but it has not been merged into `personal/main`. Upstream has also advanced by 15 commits since the integration branch was created. The safe order is to sync upstream into `personal/main`, resolve only documented ownership conflicts, and then integrate Buzz.

blockers.what: The upstream deploy-pages workflow consumes DO_SPACES_KEY and DO_SPACES_SECRET (plus bucket and endpoint settings) from GitHub Actions secrets. No consumer manifest exists, and secretctl locate correctly refused to run without a trusted supervisor context.
blockers.needs: Locate the approved CI references from a trusted context and decide whether this fork should inherit, replace, or disable the upstream Spaces upload.
steps: Decide whether kombiz/CLI-Anything should run the upstream DigitalOcean Spaces upload at all.
From an approved trusted execution context, run: secretctl locate DO_SPACES_KEY
From the same context, run: secretctl locate DO_SPACES_SECRET
If the upload remains enabled, create a complete value-free .homelab-secrets.yaml with the actual ci_job and ci_oidc delivery boundary.
Verify CI presence and delivery without printing values.

blockers.what: Greymatter has a CLI-Anything entry for a 72-command bare directory at /opt/stacks/CLI-Anything, but the entry has no GitHub identity. The estate audit therefore correctly leaves this checkout unmatched.
blockers.needs: Confirm whether the registered tool collection and this GitHub fork are the same project before assigning CLIANY identity here.
steps: Compare the registered /opt/stacks/CLI-Anything inventory with this fork without changing either authority.
Decide whether the Greymatter entry represents this repository, a generated deployment, or a separate tool collection.
If they are the same project, patch Greymatter through its reviewed registry workflow and regenerate projections.
Only after that lands, update this chapter with the confirmed identifier.

prompts.next: Work in the kombiz/CLI-Anything fork. Read AGENTS.md and FORK_POLICY.md first. Take CLIANY-FORK-002 only: fetch upstream, fast-forward the clean main mirror, merge main into personal/main, resolve conflicts according to the ownership table, and stop after the reviewed integration change is pushed. Do not modify upstream-owned behavior, integrate personal/buzz in the same change, add a Greymatter identifier, or create secret references. Verify ancestry with `git merge-base --is-ancestor main personal/main` and run checks for every conflicted path.
prompts.goal: Keep main cleanly synchronized with upstream, keep all fork-only work explicitly inventoried and reviewed through personal/main, and preserve public-repository safety. Update the four .plan files when fork state changes and publish only the exact landed personal/main revision.
